articles.title: Fed Governor Michael Barr warns AI agents could trigger bank runs in minutes
articles.source: CoinDesk: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Crypto News
articles.summary: Fed Governor Michael Barr warned that AI-driven automation could accelerate bank runs, potentially destabilizing financial systems rapidly.
articles.explain: A bank run is a crisis where everyone tries to take their money out of a bank at the same time because they fear the bank will fail. AI agents are automated software programs that can execute trades or transactions instantly. The Fed worries that if these bots are programmed to react to bad news simultaneously, they could crash a bank's liquidity faster than humans ever could.

story.title: AI Risks to Financial Stability
story.so_far: A bank run occurs when a large number of customers withdraw their deposits simultaneously due to concerns about a bank's solvency. In the digital age, mobile banking has already made this process faster. Regulators are now evaluating if autonomous AI software could amplify these runs by executing orders without human oversight.

articles.title: Hackers plant crypto-stealing code on 178 major websites, including HSBC and Ledger
articles.source: CoinDesk: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Crypto News
articles.summary: Hackers have compromised 178 major websites to inject malicious code designed to steal cryptocurrency from users.
articles.explain: A supply chain attack is when hackers infect a small part of a website's infrastructure so that visitors don't suspect anything is wrong. By placing crypto-stealing code on reputable sites, hackers can target unsuspecting users. This serves as a warning for users to be cautious even when using trusted financial websites.

story.title: Massive Website Crypto-Stealing Hack
story.so_far: Websites often use third-party tools to improve functionality, and hackers frequently target these dependencies to inject malicious scripts. This is known as a 'supply chain attack.' Users who visit these compromised sites may have their browser information or crypto-wallet access stolen without ever knowing the site was breached.

timeline.text: Major brands including HSBC and Ledger were among 178 websites affected by a malicious crypto-stealing code injection.
